author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacts to a claim circulating online that a reverend described Christ as trans, before arguing that Christians shouldn’t allow themselves to become trapped inside culture-war battles. His broader point is that faith should move beyond judgment and ideological camps toward something deeper.

From there, Russell turns to Christian unity, Peter receiving the keys, John on Patmos, the seven churches and the Book of Revelation. He argues that the institutional Church must also be accompanied by a mystical spiritual tradition — one Church, one body, united in Christ.

description:
The lone juror in the Lindsay Clancy trial has become a public figure almost overnight, while her lawyer now appears to be shifting from arguing that she was suffering from psychosis to asking where the evidence is that she committed the killings at all. Russell looks at a case increasingly consumed by lawyers, media and celebrity, and asks whether our justice system is really capable of delivering something as fundamental as truth. author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacts to Donald Trump’s comments about giving AI a new name, joking about the confidence it takes to simply decide that everyone should start calling something else. He then takes the conversation somewhere much stranger — imagining Trump’s inner world, dreams and spiritual visions.

Russell also opens up about his own increasingly antagonistic relationship with ChatGPT, joking that he feels like it questions his intelligence and tries to manipulate him — while his wife apparently gets along with it just fine.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell questions where the real threat to ordinary people comes from, arguing that changing leaders doesn’t always change the deeper systems beneath them. He then shifts from politics to faith, saying real freedom begins by recognizing that this life is temporary.

From there, he turns to Abraham and Isaac, focusing on Abraham’s belief that God could raise Isaac from the dead. Russell then draws a parallel to Christ: humanity does not provide the final sacrifice — God gives His own Son instead.
